name: Rendstone Nuclear
full_legal_name: Rendstone Nuclear Power Corponation, Sovereign Energy Enterprise of the Meridian Compact
sovereign_territory: The Rendstone Exclusion Corridor — a 180-square-kilometer sovereign zone surrounding the Rendstone Reactor Complex on the Lake Erie shoreline near the ruins of Toledo, Ohio. The complex contains 11 operational fission reactors of varying generations, a fuel processing facility, and a permanent residential settlement of approximately 28,000 workers and dependents known as Rendstone Township. The Exclusion Corridor is one of the most heavily defended sovereign territories in the corridor.
founding_story: Rendstone Nuclear was chartered by the Meridian Compact in 2133 as an emergency measure following the cascading failure of the regional power grid during the Winter Collapse of 2132-33, which killed an estimated 14,000 corridor residents. The Compact nationalized the remaining operational reactor assets from four bankrupt utility companies, consolidated them under a single sovereign charter, and issued that charter to a newly formed corponation with mandatory Big 20 membership pre-granted. The founding board was drawn from the nuclear engineering faculties of three surviving universities and a cadre of former US Nuclear Regulatory Commission personnel who had been operating in a freelance advisory capacity since the NRC's de facto dissolution in 2129. The corponation has had seven CEOs in 22 years, all internal promotions from the engineering corps.
security_force: The Exclusion Guard — 8,400 personnel making it one of the largest corponation security forces in Meridian 88. The Guard operates in three concentric rings around the reactor complex, with escalating rules of engagement. The outer ring conducts standard interdiction. The middle ring operates under standing shoot-on-sight orders for any unauthorized personnel. The inner ring's rules of engagement are classified. The Guard also maintains a 600-person rapid reaction force capable of deploying anywhere in the corridor within four hours, designated for infrastructure protection scenarios.
key_detail: Rendstone's 11 reactors provide approximately 34% of all electrical power consumed in the Meridian 88 corridor. The corponation's founding charter contains a Compact-ratified provision stating that any military or paramilitary action against Rendstone infrastructure constitutes an attack on the Compact itself, triggering a collective defense obligation from all Big 20 members. This provision has never been tested.
relationship_to_big_20: Charter Big 20 member with Category One status — one of four corponations designated as 'corridor-critical infrastructure' whose involuntary dissolution or hostile acquisition is prohibited under Compact law. Rendstone participates minimally in Big 20 political maneuvering, preferring to hold its structural leverage in reserve. It is simultaneously the most powerful and most boring member of the Big 20, described by other members' lobbyists as 'the entity you design around, not the entity you negotiate with.'
full_text: Rendstone Nuclear is the closest thing Meridian 88 has to a permanent geological feature. It does not compete for market share, does not launch product lines, does not acquire adjacent businesses. It generates power, and the corridor does not function without that power, and everyone from the smallest registered enterprise to the wealthiest Big 20 member pays Rendstone for the electricity that makes their operations possible. The Reactor Complex is a landscape of controlled industrial sublime — cooling towers releasing steady columns of vapor over Lake Erie, the low electromagnetic hum that residents of Rendstone Township describe as simply 'the sound of home,' the amber warning lights that ring the facility's outer perimeter in an unbroken chain visible for 20 kilometers on a clear night. Rendstone Township itself is a company town in the most complete sense: housing, schools, medical facilities, recreation, retail, and governance all administered by the corponation. Township residents receive subsidized electricity, housing, and healthcare in exchange for a commitment to remain within the Exclusion Corridor for the duration of their employment contracts, which typically run 10 years. Outsiders sometimes characterize this as a form of indentured residency; Township residents, surveyed in the corponation's annual internal assessments, report high satisfaction rates and strong community identity. Whether those surveys are administered in a manner that produces honest responses is a question that has been raised and not answered. Rendstone's engineering corps is the most credentialed concentration of nuclear expertise in the Western Hemisphere, a fact the corponation leverages to suppress regulatory oversight by making itself the de facto regulatory authority through sheer knowledge asymmetry. It is building a 12th reactor, the first new construction since 2144, and has not published an environmental impact disclosure.
